problem: Chats and agents could build and verify a candidate yet still leave routine protected merge/deploy as human follow-up.
root_cause: Production promotion was permitted in the autonomy contract but was not an explicit ownership obligation of the current authorized execution node. A second failure mode was observed: diverged PR merge-bases, silent missing workflow starts and over-broad regression oracles could keep valid candidates red or unstarted even after current main already contained the correct behavior.
fix: Make self-promotion mandatory after terminal-green required gates within existing authority.
Keep protected merge/deploy and production readback in the same execution tail.
Treat interruption as recoverable same-lineage work rather than a handoff to the user.
Allow only explicit hard authorization boundaries to stop autonomous production execution.
Detect zero-run PR heads as silent-start failures and retrigger the same lineage automatically.
Check current main and merge-base freshness before treating repeated CI output as current truth.
Narrow false-positive regression oracles to concrete forbidden behavior without weakening the protected invariant.
Use single-flight and same-lineage recovery to collapse duplicate queue pressure.
